messages:
tara (customer): Hey team, running into a pretty bad issue with streaming responses. When our frontend goes through our gRPC->HTTP gateway (Envoy) and uses HTTP/2, streams often stop after a few tokens. Same client code calling Redwood over plain HTTP/1.1 works fine. We get partial outputs and then the connection just closes. Anyone seen this pattern?

anna (support): Thanks for the report, Tara. Can you paste minimal repro steps and any error logs you see? Also which SDK / fetch client are you using?

tara (customer): Repro is simple: app opens SSE POST to /v1/streams with text/event-stream via gateway. Using node-fetch on the browser side (service worker). Headers we set: Authorization, Accept: text/event-stream, Content-Type: application/json.

Minimal curl (works when direct to redwood host):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"stream test"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/streams
```

When we send that to the gateway endpoint (Envoy/nginx), output comes for ~300ms then stops with no trailing event. No HTTP error code (200), connection resets on client.

josh (eng-sre): Do you see RST_STREAM or GOAWAY on the gateway side? Envoy often sends RST if upstream returns 411/length mismatch or when buffers fill. Any proxy logs?

tara (customer): Envoy logs show late: "upstream reset: connection termination" and our client sees ECONNRESET. No explicit 5xx. We also saw occasional "h2 stream closed before end of data" in the gateway.

kevin (eng-runtime): This screams buffering/trailers/chunking mismatch to me. HTTP/1.1 streaming uses chunked transfer and proxies usually just pass bytes. HTTP/2 frames can be reassembled differently; some gateways buffer until Content-Length or expect trailers. Does your gateway translate between h2 <-> h1 and insert content-length? Also any gzip or compression layer?

anna (support): Tara, can you try two quick experiments so we can triage: 1) bypass the gateway and hit Redwood directly (you already did, that works) 2) add "te: trailers" header and ensure the gateway allows transfer-encoding: chunked passthrough. Also try disabling response compression on the gateway.

tara (customer): I added "te: trailers" and set proxy_buffering off (nginx). Results: slightly better but still saw mid-stream cutoffs in ~10% of requests. Also tried forcing http/1.1 from client to gateway (no h2) — streaming is stable. So the bug only happens when client->gateway->upstream has h2 in the path.

kevin (eng-runtime): Two probable causes: 1) gRPC-gateway (or envoy) is converting stream into a unary response under some timeout or size heuristic, 2) intermediary is terminating H2 stream early because it isn't expecting indefinite streaming without content-length. Our runtime sends chunked SSE with no content-length and uses trailers for final status. If the gateway doesn't propagate trailers or disallows TE: trailers it may prematurely close.

josh (eng-sre): Can you share the Envoy config for HTTP/2 settings? In the past we've seen "max_concurrent_streams" or "stream_idle_timeout" causing early resets. Also check "http2_protocol_options: max_concurrent_streams" and "allow_connect".

tara (customer): Config excerpt (sensitive bits removed):
```yaml
http_connection_manager:
  codec_type: AUTO
  http2_protocol_options: {}
  upgrade_configs: []
  route_config: ...
  server_name: internal-gw
```
We didn't set explicit timeouts.

kevin (eng-runtime): Try setting stream_idle_timeout to a larger value and ensure connection_manager isn't using protocol conversion filters that buffer full response. Also check if your gateway has "buffer_streams" or "filter_buffering" enabled; disable it. For nginx, set proxy_request_buffering off and proxy_buffering off. For envoy, consider setting the http buffer limits to 0 for that route.

deploy-bot: Deployment to eng-runtime:investigate-streaming-bugs queued.

tara (customer): We tried adjusting idle timeouts and disabling buffering. Still reproducible at ~2% failure rate. Attached a raw tcpdump of the connection — I can paste a hexdump but it's big. Observed that on failing requests the server half-closes (FIN) without sending the SSE event delimiter or final "event: done" trailer.

kevin (eng-runtime): Can you capture and attach the exact request/response headers from the gateway for a failed run? Specifically: :method, :scheme, :authority, :path, content-length, transfer-encoding, te, content-encoding, and any x-envoy-* headers. Without trailers the client won't know final status and some clients will close if they detect malformed framing.

tara (customer): Pasted one failing header set:
```
:method: POST
:scheme: https
:authority: api.gateway.example.com
:path: /v1/streams
content-type: application/json
authorization: Bearer REDACTED
accept: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
te: trailers
user-agent: our-proxy/1.2
 x-envoy-decorator: ...
```
Response headers (truncated):
```
:status: 200
content-type: text/event-stream
content-encoding: gzip
date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 12:34:56 GMT
```
No trailers in the failed case. Upstream log shows stream ended with no trailer.

kevin (eng-runtime): Important note: We don't gzip SSE, but if the gateway is recompressing responses and setting content-encoding: gzip, it will buffer to compress which defeats streaming. That aligns with partial then stop behavior. Disable response compression on the gateway for text/event-stream.

anna (support): Action items for Tara: 1) ensure gateway not recompressing SSE responses, 2) ensure TE: trailers is propagated and allowed, 3) try adding "Connection: keep-alive" explicitly, 4) capture full proxy logs for a failing request and share.

tara (customer): Quick fix worked — turned off gzip for text/event-stream and failures dropped to near 0. Leaving TE: trailers in place as well. Thanks, this looks like gateway recompression + h2 buffering was the root cause.

kevin (eng-runtime): We'll also add a note in our docs recommending that intermediaries must: preserve TE: trailers, avoid recompressing or buffering SSE, and allow indefinite streaming without content-length. I'll file a short runbook with exact envoy/nginx snippets.

josh (eng-sre): I'll add a telemetry check in the ingress that flags if content-encoding is set for SSE responses and if trailers are absent. Might prevent regressions.

anna (support): Great — marking this resolved for now. If you see regressions, @kevin and @josh will follow up. Thanks Tara :thumbsup:

tara (customer): Thanks everyone, saved our release. :party_parrot:
